transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-13
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam Ortiz (Redwood); Dana Ruiz, Tom Becker, Aisha Khan, Victor Lee (Sparrowbridge)
Shared artifacts: renewal deck (link: https://redwood.ai/decks/sparrowbridge-renewal), draft SOW (link: https://redwood.ai/sow/sparrowbridge-draft), perf spreadsheet (link noted in chat)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for making time. Uh, quick roll call — Liam, Priya on our side; Dana, Tom, Aisha, Victor, can you hear me okay?
[00:12] Dana Ruiz: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:14] Tom Becker: good here.
[00:18] Aisha Khan: yep, all set.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Great. The goal today is a brief renewal check-in and to lock down next steps for the EU private pilot plus KMS questions that came up in email. We'll try to keep to about 40 minutes of discussion then time for procurement specifics.
[00:35] Victor Lee: sounds good. timeline wise procurement's aiming to close by end of month but we flex a couple weeks given legal back-and-forth.
[00:40] Maya Chen: understood. Just to confirm Sparrowbridge is leaning toward a 12-month renewal with an initial committed capacity and a 3-month EU private pilot?
[00:47] Dana Ruiz: yeah that's the preferred path. We want to validate latency and throughput in eu-west-1 and confirm KMS integration before we fully flip traffic.
[00:56] Liam Ortiz: perfect — we can run a targeted perf using your sample workloads. One question I had is around sequence lengths and percentiles — Dana, do your inference requests skew short or do you see long clinical narratives?
[01:10] Dana Ruiz: mostly short summaries and policy extracts, average tokens maybe 120, tail up to 800 for long claims processing notes.
[01:18] Liam Ortiz: ok that helps, we'll set bench profiles for median and p95 with that distribution. We'll also show batching impact to unit cost.
[01:25] Tom Becker: on the architecture — we're interested in Private VPC vs on-prem. Security prefers a VPC private deployment with customer-managed KMS. Can you detail support for Bring-Your-Own-KMS or HSM?
[01:37] Maya Chen: yes. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS integrations; we have docs for AWS KMS, Google KMS, and HSM connectors. Quick caveat: the private control plane will need secure peering and the keys can be stored in your KMS; Redwood's runtime doesn't persist customer keys. The security team will share a one-page KMS diagram.
[01:59] Aisha Khan: can you clarify whether encryption-at-rest keys are rotated automatically or if rotation has to happen from our side, because the audit team wants rotation proofs?
[02:10] Liam Ortiz: rotation is supported. For private deployments we can honor your rotation schedule; Redwood can request newly wrapped key material and we will rotate the data-encryption keys accordingly. There was a note in the docs where sometimes folks call KMS K-N-S in text, sorry auto-transcript noise — but the flow is standard.
[02:30] Aisha Khan: got it. also need SOC 2 and audit logs exposure.
[02:34] Maya Chen: yes, we'll include SOC 2 report and our audit logging schema. We'll also attach sample API audit logs so your auditors can validate retention windows.
[02:44] Victor Lee: procurement question — pricing. The draft we saw was a blended hosted + dedicated price. For the pilot do you have a capped pilot rate or will we be charged normal rates?
[02:56] Maya Chen: for pilots we typically provide a capped pilot discount for the first 3 months, then transition into committed reserved capacity if you elect. We'll put concrete numbers in the updated quote.
[03:06] Dana Ruiz: important — we need to understand failover behavior. If EU capacity is saturated, will requests fall back to US? That's a data residency concern.
[03:18] Liam Ortiz: good point. Redwood routing can be policy-driven. We can set hard no-fallback for sensitive routes and soft fallback for non-sensitive. For your compliance flows we recommend no-fallback and capacity alerts to trigger autoscale or queued requests.
[03:34] Tom Becker: and what about KV cache and prefix caching — is that preserved across model variants during rollouts?
[03:40] Liam Ortiz: yes, the runtime preserves KV across compatible model variants; metrics will show cache hit ratios. During canary rollouts there is a small window while caches ref warm — we'll document expected perf delta.
[03:50] Speaker 1: (murmur) can you share the benchmark set?
[03:53] Liam Ortiz: we'll pull together a perf harness and ask for a blinded sample of your corpus. Ideally 1k requests reflecting the token distribution Dana mentioned. We'll also run that under different batching settings so you can see cost vs latency tradeoffs.
[04:07] Aisha Khan: on keys again — do you support HSM-backed keys for FIPS requirements?
[04:12] Maya Chen: yes, HSM via customer HSM or cloud HSM is supported for private deployment. We'll note the providers we validated against in the KMS doc.
[04:21] Victor Lee: legal will want to see SLAs; what's your standard latency SLO in dedicated EU pools?
[04:28] Maya Chen: we offer SLA-backed latency targets per model class for Dedicated customers — typical p95 token latency targets are in the mid single-digit ms per token on our optimized kernels, but that depends on model and sequence length. We'll put expected numbers from previous similar customers into the quote.
[04:43] Dana Ruiz: okay. Any technical caveats for quantized model variants? We sometimes use quantized models to reduce cost.
[04:50] Liam Ortiz: quantization helps cost but can change output characteristics. For inference we support int8 / nf4 variants; we'll recommend evaluation prompts to check quality regressions. We can host both versions and provide canary rollouts.
[05:01] Tom Becker: timebox — schedule and actions?
[05:05] Maya Chen: proposed schedule: updated quote & SOW by next Tuesday (1/20), perf run scheduled for week of 1/25, security artifacts by 1/18, procurement review week of 1/26. Does that align?
[05:17] Victor Lee: yes that aligns. We'll aim to have legal look at SOW quickly.
[05:20] Aisha Khan: I'll send our retention policy and the PII redaction checklist after this call.
[05:26] Liam Ortiz: perfect. For the perf run we'll need IAM creds for a read-only dataset S3 bucket or equivalent. We'll share the runbook after we confirm scope.
[05:36] Dana Ruiz: also please call out egress estimates into EU — that matters for pricing.
[05:40] Maya Chen: good callout; egress and cross-region replication will be explicit in the quote.
[05:44] Tom Becker: curious — what's the typical cold-start behavior for your private runtime? We saw some spikes during canaries with other vendors.
[05:52] Liam Ortiz: we mitigate with continuous batching and prefix caching; cold-starts are mostly at node addition events. For private pools we advise small steady baseline capacity to minimize node churn during business hours. We can model node utilization and expected tail latencies in the perf readout.
[06:07] Victor Lee: procurement question — are there any one-off setup fees for VPC peering and KMS integration?
[06:12] Maya Chen: there's usually an initial onboarding fee for private deployments to cover secure peering, runbook integration, and 1:1 ops onboarding. We'll itemize it in the SOW. For some enterprise deals we amortize that into the first term.
[06:24] Dana Ruiz: okay that helps.
[06:27] Maya Chen: quick recap then: Redwood to send updated quote + SOW with pilot pricing and egress line items (Maya), security to share SOC2 + KMS/HSM integration diagram (Maya/Liam), SE to schedule perf run and share runbook (Liam), Sparrowbridge to share PII retention/redaction docs (Aisha), procurement to confirm PO timeline (Victor).
[06:46] Victor Lee: yes. Let's plan a follow-up in two weeks after perf run results.
[06:51] Maya Chen: perfect — we'll send calendar invite and the doc pack. Thanks everyone.
[06:55] Dana Ruiz: thanks.
[06:57] Transcript end. Note: occasional transcription errors in product names (e.g., "KV cache" was transcribed as "K-V cache") and acronyms; please rely on attachments for exact specs.
